thesis: 进入生产的 Agent，往往并不追求高度自主。
takeaways: 任务窄、工作流短，允许分钟级延迟
使用现成模型、明确工具和静态流程
通常在 10 步以内交给人类确认
评估失败、拒答、越权和交接，而不只看答案质量
contrarian: 生产团队正在主动牺牲一部分自主性，换取可控性与可靠性。这与“越 Agentic 越先进”的常见叙事几乎相反。

items.title: 生产环境里的 Agent 实际长什么样？
items.summary: 对 20 个部署团队、306 名从业者及 86 个已进入试点或生产的 Agent 系统的调查显示：多数团队直接使用现成模型、人工设计 Prompt，并把工作流控制在人工介入前 10 步以内。
items.design: 用户任务 → 明确工具集 → 短流程执行 → 人工检查或接管。
items.evidence: 数据直接来自部署团队，但更可能覆盖成功或已进入试点的项目，可能低估失败项目。
items.idea: 寻找一个人工需要 20–60 分钟、但允许 AI 花几分钟完成的窄任务，在最后一步交给人确认。

image.alt: 生产 Agent 调查中的验证方法共现图
image.caption: 部署团队组合多种验证方法，并普遍保留人工检查与短工作流。

items.title: 与其让搜索一次决定答案，不如让模型继续调查
items.summary: AgenticRAG 保留企业已有搜索系统，只增加 search、find、open、summarize 四个工具，让模型在发现证据不足时重新查询，而不是被第一次检索结果锁死。
items.design: 一次搜索变为可迭代的“检索 → 进入文档 → 检查证据 → 再检索”。
items.evidence: 多个公开基准表现强，但尚未充分展示真实运行成本、用户采纳和长期维护负担。
items.idea: 把普通 FAQ 缩窄为跨多份文档、需要比较来源并判断证据是否充分的调查任务。

image.alt: Microsoft AgenticRAG 的迭代调查循环图
image.caption: 模型通过搜索、进入文档和检查证据循环调查，而非接受一次检索的结果。

items.title: 企业 RAG 最危险的错误，可能是检索到无权看的正确答案
items.summary: 相关性排序并不等于权限判断。多部门、多客户环境中，语义最相关的文档可能恰好属于另一个租户；权限检查必须进入写入、检索、工具执行与对话状态的每一层。
items.design: 权限标签写入 → 检索时 ABAC 过滤 → 服务端管理 Agent 状态与工具权限 → 共享模型推理。
items.evidence: 受控测试中的检索层门控阻止了全部跨租户泄露，但真实企业的权限规则维护更复杂。
items.idea: 做一个带权限过滤记录的共享知识助手，把“只使用当前用户有权访问的证据”设为核心能力。

image.alt: 多租户权限感知 RAG 的参考架构图
image.caption: 租户身份和角色过滤进入检索层，降低跨租户证据泄漏风险。

items.title: 企业已有的客服对话，可以变成知识库与评估数据
items.summary: 先给历史对话评分并剔除错误与矛盾，再提取结构化知识作为 RAG 的唯一来源，同时用历史对话生成用户模拟器，测试回答、拒答与转人工能力。
items.design: 对话质检 → 知识提取 → 受治理的 RAG → 用户模拟 → 拒答与转人工测试。
items.evidence: 在两个领域可安全自动处理约 30% 电话，但主要依赖模拟用户，尚非长期真实客户部署。
items.idea: 从历史工单中提取可复用知识，只自动处理高置信度的重复问题，并评估何时应该拒答。

image.alt: 客户服务知识提取与自动处理结果图表
image.caption: 历史对话经过质检、知识提取和模拟评估后，只自动处理高置信度问题。

items.title: Agent 上线前，可以从规则自动生成一场“驾照考试”
items.summary: 先定义 Agent 的操作边界：能访问什么、执行什么、何时必须停止，再从行业规则自动生成正常、边缘和攻击场景，最终形成部署判定。
items.design: 行业规则与本体 → 自动生成测试场景 → 多模型执行 → 汇总证据 → 批准、条件批准或拒绝。
items.evidence: 覆盖 1,800 个场景，但方法优势在严格统计校正后并不显著；通过测试也不等于开放环境绝对安全。
items.idea: 给定 Agent 的权限、工具与企业规则，自动生成上线前测试，并判断它是否可以部署。

image.alt: Agent 上线测试的跨模型评估热力图
image.caption: 规则生成的正常、边缘与攻击场景共同形成上线前的证据矩阵。

projectIdeas.title: 窄任务调查型 Agent
projectIdeas.description: 围绕一个具体业务问题，用 3–4 个受控工具完成多步调查，输出明确格式，最终由人确认。

projectIdeas.title: AI 上线前测试系统
projectIdeas.description: 检查另一个 AI 是否引用正确证据、访问越权资料、该拒答时拒答，并在正确节点交给人工。

translation.title: What Do Agents in Production Actually Look Like?
translation.summary: A survey of 20 deployment teams, 306 practitioners, and 86 agent systems already in pilot or production shows that most teams use off-the-shelf models, write prompts by hand, and keep workflows within 10 steps before human intervention.
translation.design: User task → defined toolset → short workflow → human review or takeover.
translation.evidence: The data come directly from deployment teams, but may be more likely to cover successful projects or those already in pilot, potentially undercounting failed projects.
translation.idea: Find a narrow task that takes a person 20–60 minutes but allows AI a few minutes to complete it, then have a person confirm the final step.

image.alt: Co-occurrence chart of validation methods in the production-agent survey
image.caption: Deployment teams combine multiple validation methods and generally retain human review and short workflows.

translation.title: Instead of Letting One Search Decide the Answer, Let the Model Keep Investigating
translation.summary: AgenticRAG keeps an enterprise's existing search system and adds only four tools—search, find, open, and summarize—so the model can query again when it finds insufficient evidence, rather than being locked into the first retrieval result.
translation.design: A single search becomes an iterative cycle of retrieval → opening documents → checking evidence → searching again.
translation.evidence: It performs strongly on several public benchmarks, but real operating costs, user adoption, and long-term maintenance burden have not yet been sufficiently demonstrated.
translation.idea: Narrow an ordinary FAQ into an investigation that spans multiple documents, requires comparing sources, and judges whether the evidence is sufficient.

image.alt: Diagram of Microsoft AgenticRAG's iterative investigation loop
image.caption: The model investigates through a cycle of search, opening documents, and checking evidence instead of accepting the result of a single retrieval.

translation.title: The Most Dangerous Enterprise RAG Error May Be Retrieving a Correct Answer the User Is Not Authorized to See
translation.summary: Relevance ranking is not an access-control decision. In an environment with multiple departments and customers, the most semantically relevant document may belong to another tenant. Permission checks must be built into every layer: ingestion, retrieval, tool execution, and conversation state.
translation.design: Attach permission labels at ingestion → apply ABAC filters during retrieval → manage agent state and tool permissions on the server → run inference with a shared model.
translation.evidence: Retrieval-layer gating prevented all cross-tenant leaks in controlled tests, but maintaining permission rules in a real enterprise is more complex.
translation.idea: Build a shared knowledge assistant with a record of permission filtering, making ‘use only evidence the current user is authorized to access’ its core capability.

image.alt: Reference architecture diagram for permission-aware, multi-tenant RAG
image.caption: Tenant identity and role filters enter the retrieval layer, reducing the risk of cross-tenant evidence leaks.

translation.title: An Enterprise's Existing Customer-Service Conversations Can Become a Knowledge Base and Evaluation Data
translation.summary: First score historical conversations and remove errors and contradictions. Then extract structured knowledge as the sole source for RAG, while using past conversations to create user simulators that test answers, refusals, and handoffs to human agents.
translation.design: Conversation quality checks → knowledge extraction → governed RAG → user simulation → refusal and human-handoff tests.
translation.evidence: About 30% of calls could be handled safely and automatically in two domains, but the result relied mainly on simulated users rather than a long-term deployment with real customers.
translation.idea: Extract reusable knowledge from historical support tickets, automate only high-confidence recurring questions, and evaluate when the assistant should refuse to answer.

image.alt: Chart of customer-service knowledge extraction and automated handling results
image.caption: After historical conversations undergo quality checks, knowledge extraction, and simulated evaluation, only high-confidence questions are handled automatically.
